groups.label: Inscribed angles on the same arc

statements.text: In the same circle, the measures of all inscribed angles subtended by the same arc are equal in measure.
In the same circle or in congruent circles, the measures of the inscribed angles subtended by arcs of equal measures are equal.
In the circle M, if $m(\widehat{AC}) = m(\widehat{DF})$ then $m(\angle B) = m(\angle E)$. Formula: $m(\widehat{AC}) = m(\widehat{DF}) \Rightarrow m(\angle B) = m(\angle E)$
For any two circles M and N, if $m(\widehat{AC}) = m(\widehat{DF})$ then $m(\angle B) = m(\angle E)$. Formula: $m(\widehat{AC}) = m(\widehat{DF}) \Rightarrow m(\angle B) = m(\angle E)$
Converse of the previous corollary (point 3): in the same circle or in congruent circles, inscribed angles of equal measures subtend arcs of equal measures.

The converse of theorem 2: if two angles are subtended to the same base and on the same side of it, and have the same measure, then their vertices lie on an arc of a circle and the base is a chord in it.
